Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not consistently apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to request paths that differ only by a trailing slash. This may allow an authenticated user who holds a broader delete permission on system configuration paths to disable a secrets engine, auth method, or audit device that a more specific deny rule was intended to protect. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93335) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows authenticated users with stacks:create permission to read sensitive files by supplying an arbitrary composePath during stack adoption. Attackers can adopt a stack pointing to the encryption key, SQLite database, or /proc/self/environ and read it via the compose endpoint to obtain all stored credentials.

AiSOC 12.1.0 before 23.3.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to query the enrichment service through Next.js console rewrite routes. Attackers can send requests to /api/v1/enrichment/lookup or /api/v1/enrichment/bulk to retrieve threat-intelligence results and set force to true to consume commercial provider API quota.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to access another user's private mail by supplying a crafted reloadMailTypeId parameter to Ctrl::getCurObj() without a readRight() ownership check in CtrlMail.php. Attackers can manipulate the mail identifier value, such as reloadMailTypeId=mail-1, to retrieve the title and body of private messages belonging to other users, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive communications.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can submit an error-based extractvalue payload through personsSort to leak database information, such as the MariaDB version, via the user and space listing pages.

Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to letter case variants of user and group names in auth methods that treat these names as case-insensitive. This may allow an authenticated user with delegated permissions to modify a protected user or group, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-128100) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault's Login MFA feature did not consistently enforce the lifetime of pending two-phase login requests. This may allow a user who previously completed the first authentication factor to complete MFA and obtain a Vault token after the pending request should have expired, including after the user's primary credential has been rotated. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92738) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.26.

Frappe CRM before 1.84.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the get_deal_contacts method that allows authenticated low-privileged users to read contacts of deals they cannot access. Attackers can supply or iterate CRM Deal names to obtain linked contacts' full names, email addresses, and mobile numbers, bypassing row-level permission rules.
Improper authorization in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Phison E12 and E18 PCIe SSD controllers contain a Secure Boot bypass vulnerability that allows a privileged local attacker to inject persistent boot-patch tuples into the unsigned, CRC-protected flash ID page read by the BootROM. By overwriting a fuse-derived RAM variable via a crafted patch entry using Phison Vendor Specific Commands, an attacker can force CRC-only firmware verification instead of signature checking, enabling an unsigned firmware image to load and creating a persistent controller-level implant that survives firmware reinstallation and operates below the host operating system.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain a Download of Code Without Integrity Check vulnerability. A highly privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code execution.

Incorrect authorization in SiteSettings in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker leveraging social engineering to bypass system access restrictions via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Low)

Race condition in DevTools in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker leveraging social engineering to bypass web origin policy into a privileged page via a crafted Chrome extension. (Chromium security severity: Low)

Typecho before 1.3.1-rc contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the XML-RPC pingback.ping method where checkSafeHost() validates a hostname's resolved IP once but the subsequent outbound request performs an independent DNS resolution, creating a TOCTOU window exploitable via DNS rebinding. An unauthenticated attacker can configure a domain to return a benign IP at validation time and an internal address (loopback, RFC1918, or cloud metadata IP) at request time, causing the server to issue blind SSRF requests to arbitrary internal hosts and ports.

SmarterTools SmarterMail Missing Authorization Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of SmarterTools SmarterMail. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of email attachments. The issue results from the lack of authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to disclose sensitive information in the context of a target user. Was ZDI-CAN-33567.

Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Observable Discrepancy Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the HomeKit Authentication service, which listens on TCP port 8080 by default. When processing crafted pairing requests, the service discloses internal information via an observable discrepancy between possible responses. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28470.

Poppler through 26.11.0 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in the libcurl-based remote file loader that trusts unvalidated HEAD Content-Length values in CurlCachedFileLoader::init(). Malicious HTTP servers can return an enormous Content-Length so CachedFile resizes its chunk cache accordingly, aborting pdfinfo or PDFDocFactory-based applications with std::bad_alloc for denial of service.

A SQL injection vulnerability affects an administrative API in HCL Commerce versions 8, 9.0.1 and 9.1.0 - 9.1.21.  A remote attacker with an administrative role could use a crafted URL to infer unauthorized data from the database.

Pleasanter contains an issue with insertion of sensitive information into sent data in the API. If the affected product receives a specially crafted API request sent by a remote authenticated attacker, the authentication credentials of other users, including administrators, such as API keys, may be obtained. As a result, the attacker may perform arbitrary operations on the affected product with the privileges associated with the obtained credentials.
Tanium addressed an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in Tanium Client.

Relative path traversal in the object detection dataset preparation tool in AutoGluon Multimodal before 1.6.0 might allow adversary-in-the-middle attackers to write arbitrary files with the privileges of the user running the tool via a crafted dataset archive substituted for a dataset downloaded over plaintext HTTP.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade autogluon.multimodal to version 1.6.0 or later.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated observer-level users to sort software listings by arbitrary columns via the order_key parameter. Attackers can order by joined hosts table columns such as node keys and use pagination as a binary-search oracle to extract sensitive column values.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the settings.getWebServerSettings protected procedure returns the complete global web-server settings object to any authenticated member, including the stored sshPrivateKey, even though settings.saveSSHPrivateKey requires an administrator. A default member can therefore retrieve infrastructure, deployment, or server-management credentials that only an administrator can configure. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to inject SQL via unescaped clientid values in the wsapp_map webservice operation. Attackers can register a sync application with wsapp_register, then send delete-mode entries with quoted clientid values processed by SyncServer.php to extract database contents including administrator access keys.

Meilisearch before 1.55.1 and 1.56.x before 1.56.1 contains a quadratic memory consumption vulnerability in filter-parser that allows attackers with a search API key to exhaust server memory. Attackers can send a roughly 100 KB filter, such as a _geoPolygon with thousands of coordinates, to the search endpoint, crashing the server and taking all indexes offline.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in MP4Box because gf_sg_reset frees DEF'd proto sub-graph nodes without removing them from the GF_Proto node_code list. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with nested PROTOs so gf_sg_proto_del unregisters freed nodes during teardown, crashing MP4Box and corrupting the heap.

SDDC Manager contains a local privilege-escalation vulnerability.
Affected versions: 9.1.x.x (fixed in 9.1.1.0200); 9.0.x.x (fixed in 9.0.2.0100); 5.x (fixed in 5.2.5).

VMware Tools for Windows contains a SAML token signature bypass vulnerability.
Affected versions: 13.x.x.x (fixed in 13.1.5.0); 12.3.x (fixed in 12.5.5).

A flaw was found in Moodle's Blackboard question import format. Insufficient validation of file paths during the question import process allows an authenticated user with permissions to import questions into a question bank to read arbitrary files accessible to the web server process. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to view sensitive files, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.

THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

In ConnectWise Automate versions prior to
2026.11, a condition in Web Control Center (WCC2) authorization handling could
allow an authenticated contact user to access information associated with other
clients on the same Automate server through API requests. This may result in
disclosure of information outside the user’s assigned access scope. The issue
is limited to information disclosure and does not extend existing modification
or command execution permissions. This issue is resolved in ConnectWise
Automate 2026.11.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use the apps backup and restore Representational State Transfer (REST) API to prevent subsequent apps backup or restore operations until Splunk Enterprise restarts. This could result in a Denial of Service (DoS).
The vulnerability is possible because the apps backup and restore REST API handlers do not correctly enforce authorization.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user that holds a role with the list_deployment_server capability could access sensitive information from inputs.conf files outside the intended deployment app directory through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API does not restrict a deployment app name to an existing deployment app before reading input configurations.
For more information see authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.4-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf), Deployment server architecture (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/update-your-deployment/9.0/deployment-server-and-forwarder-management/deployment-server-architecture), and inputs.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.16-configuration-file-reference/inputs.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could store attacker-controlled data in finding exclusion rule metadata. Another authenticated user could later open the Finding Exclusion Rules page. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who opened the page. The first user could access data and perform actions available to the later user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not escape backslashes in finding exclusion rule metadata before adding the values to a page search.
For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the edit_modinput_identity_manager capability could use Asset and Identity Management to modify protected saved searches and role capabilities. With this access, the user could obtain full administrator access to the Splunk platform.
The vulnerability is possible because Asset and Identity Management does not validate the app namespace before sending a Representational State Transfer (REST) API request with a system authentication token.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Add asset and identity data to Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/asset-and-identity-management/add-asset-and-identity-data-to-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the containers:view permission could access automation history for containers outside the label or tenant scope assigned to the user. This could expose action parameters, connector result summaries, and other investigation and response activity.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk SOAR Representational State Transfer (REST) API checks the permission to view containers but does not restrict automation history to containers within the label or tenant scope assigned to the user.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user whose role grants system_settings:view but not assets:view could access asset and application inventory, tenant identifiers, connector run messages, and stored configuration snapshots through the ingestion status Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the ingestion status REST API checks the system_settings:view permission but does not enforce assets:view or tenant restrictions before it returns asset-derived ingestion records.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.3.1/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.4.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), and Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.1/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who can edit and run playbooks could cause automation batches for other events to stop running.
The vulnerability occurs because Splunk SOAR does not bind playbook API requests to the server-provided execution context.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a Splunk SOAR user who can edit and run playbooks for a permitted container label could associate action and callback state with a running playbook outside that container label. This could affect playbook automation for containers that the user cannot view.
The vulnerability is possible because the Playbook Automation API accepts a supplied playbook run identifier without verifying that it is bound to the server-provided playbook execution context.
The vulnerability requires a running playbook on a container label that the user cannot view.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who can edit and run a playbook on a permitted label could cause Splunk SOAR to return custom-function status and callback state from another playbook run.
The issue results from insufficient binding between a custom-function-status request and the playbook run that initiates it.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who can edit and run playbooks on a container label could associate a custom-function callback with another playbook run. The callback could modify the state of a container outside the authorized scope for that user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not bind playbook API requests to the trusted playbook run and container context.

In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, a user who can read splunkd_access.log or the _internal Splunk index could recover the Stream forwarder authentication key and use it to impersonate a trusted Stream forwarder.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk App for Stream sends the authentication key in an internal request URL, and Splunk records that URL in splunkd_access.log.
For more information see About Splunk Stream (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.1/introduction/about-splunk-stream) and restmap.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.3-configuration-file-reference/restmap.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use the search jobs Representational State Transfer (REST) API to access indexed events that the srchFilter setting for the role should hide. The same user could also run internal Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and bypass SPL safeguards for risky commands within indexes that the role can search.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape required field values before it includes them in an internally generated search.
For more information, see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/rest-api-reference/9.4/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions), authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.5-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf), and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands).

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could determine whether a username exists through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API or Splunk Web and lock out existing user accounts through repeated login attempts.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise returns different login failure responses for locked existing user accounts and nonexistent usernames.

The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library improperly synchronizes authentication credentials set on a shared HTTP client during request execution. When concurrent requests are dispatched for different principals, one principal's credential may be transmitted on an outbound request intended for another principal, which can result in credential exposure and lead to unauthorized actions performed as the affected principal at the Okta Management API.

On Intel-based macOS systems, the Okta Device Access (ODA) component of Okta Verify for macOS configures a LaunchDaemon service whose program path resolves via a symbolic link in /usr/local/bin. In environments where non-standard directory permissions grant local non-root users write access to this path, the symbolic link target can be modified, causing the LaunchDaemon to execute the replacement binary upon service restart.
IEEE 1609.2 protocol dissector crash in 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 and 4.4.0 to 4.4.19 allows denial of service

A SQL injection vulnerability when the recipient tapped on a specially crafted “order details” message from an unofficial client in WhatsApp for Android prior to version 2.26.35.74 could have allowed deletion of locally-stored WhatsApp files and, only if the user is online at time of receipt, leaked one bit of information asked by the attacker about the user’s chat database via an induced-crash delivery receipt timing sidechannel. We have not seen evidence of exploitation in the wild.
U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program stores local user passwords as unsalted MD5 hashes. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

Open Robotics RViz PointCloud2Display PointField Out-of-Bounds Read Denial-of-Service Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of Open Robotics RViz. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of PointCloud2 messages. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a read past the end of an allocated object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create a denial-of-service condition on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-32123.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/requestPasswordReset calls deleteTokens by user ID before creating a reset token, while password-reset and email-verification records in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/token.ts have no populated flow type. When password reset is enabled and email verification is enforced, an unauthenticated attacker who knows a target email can repeatedly delete pending verification tokens and prevent account verification until the unverified account expires. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

WPC Smart Messages for WooCommerce plugin before 4.3.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor or Author privileges to disclose arbitrary post meta and private product data by supplying attacker-controlled id and key attributes to the [wpcsm_product_field] and [wpcsm_product_data] shortcodes without any capability or protected-meta checks. Attackers can embed these shortcodes in a published post to exfiltrate sensitive order data such as billing email, phone, and address stored as post meta, as well as private or draft product descriptions and purchase notes, exposing confidential customer and business information to unauthenticated site visitors.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.9, GET /api/permissions/search-principals passes the q parameter to JavaScript RegExp construction and MongoDB regex queries in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/userGroup.ts findGroupsByNamePattern and searchPrincipals without escaping metacharacters. An authenticated user with people-picker permission can submit a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that blocks the Node.js event loop and makes the service unresponsive to concurrent users; invalid patterns can also produce server errors. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.9.

A cross-origin issue was addressed with improved tracking of security origins. This issue is fixed in iOS 26.7.2 and iPadOS 26.7.2. Processing maliciously crafted web content may disclose sensitive user information.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent placeholders in a shortcode attribute from being expanded with unescaped nested shortcode output, allowing users with a role as low as contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not escape the error message returned when a remote feed cannot be retrieved before outputting it, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators by pointing the feed at a server they control.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict which PHP functions a shortcode's filter attribute can call, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to remove WordPress' term-slug sanitization and perform SQL injection attacks through another shortcode's taxonomy term attribute.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict the content type of its lightbox shortcode, allowing users with the contributor role and above to make the lightbox fetch HTML from an attacker-controlled server and insert it into the page unsanitised, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting when a user opens the lightbox.

The Shortcodes Ultimate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in versions up to, and including, 7.9.1 This is due to su_get_current_url() interpolating the raw Host request header into the authority portion of a URL that is then passed to esc_url() — which by design preserves '[' and ']' inside the authority so IPv6 literal hosts remain valid — and the [su_qrcode] shortcode substituting that value into its data attribute (the documented %CURRENT_URL% token) before feeding it to do_shortcode(). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include arbitrary PHP files that reside within the active theme's root directory (bounded because '/' inside an attribute value terminates parse_url()'s host and is then percent-encoded and stripped), and — when the shipped-default 'Unsafe features' option remains on — to read arbitrary post meta of any post, on any front-end page that renders [su_qrcode data="%CURRENT_URL%"].

The HUSKY – Products Filter for WooCommerce Professional plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'link (inner 'woof_text' query parameter)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.7 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The exploit requires a valid product_messenger nonce, which is issued by the woof_redraw_woof AJAX endpoint to any visitor when the shortcode's by_only attribute is set — an attribute that can itself be forced via the attacker-controlled woof_shortcode request parameter, making the nonce trivially obtainable by any logged-in user.

The Unlimited Elements For Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.26 via the getFileContentByUrl function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The nonce protecting the get_addon_output_data AJAX endpoint is emitted on the Elementor editor page, which is accessible to Contributors, making the endpoint reachable by any authenticated user at that privilege level or above.

The WP Job Portal – AI-Powered Recruitment System for Company or Job Board website plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'columns[<attacker-chosen key>]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.0 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

When the last EoE fragment has the TIME_APPEND flag set, the handler subtracts 4 from rxframeoffset to strip the timestamp. There is no check that rxframeoffset is at least 4. A fragment carrying fewer than 4 bytes of payload that is also marked LAST causes rxframeoffset to wrap to 0xFFFFFFFC, which is then stored as the buffer length and handed to the TCP/IP stack.

A CoE SDO request for index 0xFFFF matches the object list terminator entry instead of returning not-found. The terminator has a NULL objdesc pointer. Callers dereference it without checking, crashing the slave.

sizeOfPDO, called during state transitions, uses the subindex-0 count of the SM-assign and PDO-mapping objects as loop bounds without checking those counts against the descriptor array sizes. On builds where those subindex-0 values are writable via SDO, a master can write 0xFF and cause sizeOfPDO to read past the end of the descriptor arrays on the next transition to SAFEOP.

The FoE file table allows entries to omit a write handler by setting write_function to NULL, making the file read-only. FOE_fopen did not check whether write_function was present before accepting a write request; a master sending a WRQ for a read-only file caused a call through a NULL function pointer.

The EoE receive and transmit paths call the handle_recv_buffer and fetch_send_buffer callbacks without first checking whether they are set. Both callbacks are documented as optional; an application that omits either one causes a call through a NULL function pointer when the first EoE frame arrives or when the transmit polling loop runs.

Admidio before 5.0.18 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in mylist.php that loads list configurations by the list_uuid parameter while checking only the organization, not the owner or private flag. Authenticated users with Lists module access who know a victim's list UUID can read its name, selected profile fields, sort order and filter conditions.

Admidio from 5.0.2 before 5.0.17 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows any logged-in member to read server files by placing local paths in img src attributes of eCard messages. Attackers can send an eCard to their own account so sendEcard() embeds files like adm_my_files/config.php via addEmbeddedImage(), disclosing database credentials and /etc/passwd.

Vikunja from 2.4.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the richtext converter that allows authenticated project writers to exhaust server memory and CPU by storing tables with unbounded rowspan and colspan values. Any project reader or CalDAV client can trigger the expansion through markdown task reads, CalDAV GETs, or the frontend editor, producing 100 MB responses from a 64-byte description.

Vikunja from 0.18.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource amplification vulnerability in pkg/models/export.go that allows authenticated users to exhaust server memory by exporting heavily related tasks. Attackers can relate many tasks to one task with a large description and request a user export, causing an out-of-memory crash for all users.

Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to crash the server by uploading extreme-width images as task attachments. Attackers can request the attachment preview endpoint so Lanczos resampling allocates width-proportional weight tables, OOM-killing the process repeatedly with sub-megabyte PNGs.

Vikunja from 2.6.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the Planka migration converter that multiplies task allocations for duplicate list IDs. Attackers controlling a Planka server can return boards with duplicate list IDs and many cards to exhaust memory and OOM-kill the Vikunja process.

Vikunja from 0.8.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated project readers to amplify response size by repeating requested properties in CalDAV PROPFIND requests. Attackers can send PROPFIND requests to the dav projects endpoint with hundreds of duplicate calendar-data properties to exhaust server memory, CPU, and bandwidth.

Vikunja 2.3.0 before 2.8.0 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation in the CSV migration module because it does not de-duplicate label column mappings or cap labels per row, and enforces the item limit only after the full import is built. Authenticated users can send one request to /api/v2/migration/csv/migrate with repeated label mappings or many labels per row, exhausting memory until the server is OOM-killed.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows clients with table write access to persist writes refused by THROWing table events within interactive transactions. Attackers can run a guarded statement via RPC begin and query, ignore the returned error, and commit to persist the record and event side effects.

SurrealDB 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 includes the record id of a referencing row in the error returned when a delete is blocked by an ON DELETE REJECT reference, without checking the caller's SELECT permission on that row. An authenticated principal with DELETE permission can attempt to delete a referenced record and read the rejection error to learn the existence and exact ids of referencing records hidden by row-level SELECT permissions.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a permission bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege database users to read restricted records by calling the GET /export endpoint. Attackers can export raw records that skip table SELECT predicates and field-level SELECT permissions, exposing other users' rows and hidden fields.

better-auth 1.3.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the admin plugin's /admin/update-user endpoint that lets roles holding user:update change another user's phoneNumber and phoneNumberVerified fields. Attackers can set their own verified phone number on a higher-privileged account and sign in via phone OTP to take it over.

Better Auth (better-auth, @better-auth/kysely-adapter, and @better-auth/drizzle-adapter) before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition with MySQL or MariaDB serial IDs because the inserted row's ID is read via a separate LAST_INSERT_ID() query that may run on a different pooled connection. Under concurrent load, a user signing in can receive another user's session and act as that user.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read schema definitions of denied types through listings ignoring per-type ACLs. Attackers can query the PostgreSQL wire catalog, GraphQL introspection, or MCP get_schema to reveal property names, indexes, inheritance, and materialized view SQL.

ArcadeDB from 26.7.1 before 26.11.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because LSMTreeFullTextIndex computes BM25 corpus statistics over all buckets of the indexed type, ignoring bucket access control on subtypes. Authenticated users with read access to a supertype but not its subtype can run EXPLAIN or PROFILE on full-text queries and read totalDocs and per-term df values to count hidden subtype documents containing chosen terms.

actix-http 3.18.10 before 3.20.2 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in its chunked decoder, which treats a bare LF after the last chunk as the start of a trailer section. Attackers can send a body ending in 0\r\n\n through a connection-reusing proxy so the next request's body is parsed as new requests, bypassing WAF or upstream protections.

Heym before 0.0.148 passes Playwright navigate-step URLs to page.goto() without validating the scheme and runs step-based scripts inside the backend container. A signed-in user who can run workflows can navigate to file:// URLs and use getText to read known-path files such as the Kubernetes ServiceAccount token or Docker secrets.

Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.21, 2.30.0 before 2.34.10, 2.35.0 before 2.35.8, 2.36.0 before 2.36.5, and 2.37.0 before 2.37.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the workspace agent dRPC API, whose handlers dereference unset request sub-messages and unconfigured Tailnet providers without recovering from panics. Attackers holding a workspace agent token can send UpdateLifecycle, UpdateStartup, or BatchUpdateMetadata messages lacking sub-messages, or call RefreshResumeToken or WorkspaceUpdates, to repeatedly crash coderd.

Frappe 8.8.0 before 16.30.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the SMS Settings get_contact_number API that lets attackers read any Contact's phone numbers without permission checks. Attackers can call the endpoint, which uses an uncorrelated EXISTS subquery, to retrieve mobile_no and phone values of arbitrary Contact records, exposing PII.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to perform state-changing actions by exploiting missing Origin header validation and absent CSRF tokens. Attackers can lure authenticated users to a same-site attacker page that submits forged POST requests to stop, start, or delete stacks, modify settings, and change credentials.

Dockhand before 1.0.50 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows authenticated unprivileged users to read restricted data by querying API endpoints lacking RBAC checks. Attackers can access /api/users, /api/license, and /api/hawser/connect to obtain user emails and roles, the full license key, and environment details, while an invalid license grants all users admin rights.

Hysteria 2.5.0 before 2.8.2 contains a memory allocation vulnerability when sniffing is enabled, allowing authenticated users to trigger out-of-memory conditions. Attackers with a valid password can forward a crafted QUIC packet with a huge crypto length, causing the server to exhaust memory and crash.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a double free vulnerability in the XMT-A scene loader that leaves a stale GF_Command pointer in a Conditional node's SFCommandBuffer when the buffer element is not properly closed. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file with malformed nesting, causing gf_sg_sfcommand_del() to free the live command, corrupting heap memory and crashing the process.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that retains a pointer to a PROTO sub-graph freed by gf_sg_proto_del(). Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file imported with MP4Box, causing xmt_parse_command() to update the freed graph's referencing_commands list and crash the process.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in xmt_resolve_od_links() that allows attackers to corrupt stack memory via over-long object descriptor URL fragments. Attackers can craft an XMT scene file whose URL fragment overflows the fixed 5000-byte szURL buffer via sprintf, crashing MP4Box when a user loads it.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory when xmt_node_end() discards an out-of-scope node without resetting command-buffer state. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file that leaves parser->command_buffer and parser->command dangling, causing later parsing to access freed memory and crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT-A scene loader that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted XMT files. Attackers can persuade a user to process an XMT file whose discarded out-of-scope nodes cause gf_node_unregister() to dereference a freed child, crashing the process.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_resolve_od_links() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to read freed heap memory via stale strstr() pointers. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file whose MFURL field contains an entry without a URL string, causing sprintf() to read freed memory and crash the process.

Servas before 1.2.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to modify and delete other users' data by supplying target resource ids. Attackers can abuse TagController update and destroy, LinkController destroy, and GroupController destroy actions to rename or delete tags and delete links and groups.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in gf_odm_disconnect() in src/compositor/object_manager.c caused by a deferred scene_ns_remove_object task holding a raw object manager pointer. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene whose commands delete a Background2D node, freeing the object manager early to crash the process and corrupt heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to access freed heap memory via stale object descriptor links. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene where xmt_node_end() frees a subtree containing InputSensor MFURL fields, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory and crash MP4Box.

Freedit before 0.9.9 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the edit_post_post handler for POST /post/edit/:pid that skips ownership and status checks when a Private inn is submitted. Members of a Private inn can overwrite any post by sequential id, including moderator-locked posts, re-attributing it to themselves and destroying original content.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in scene graph teardown that allows attackers to trigger access to freed memory via crafted scene files. A node shared across multiple PROTO node_code lists is freed by gf_sg_reset(), and gf_sg_proto_del() then calls gf_node_unregister() on the dangling pointer, crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that leaves freed node URL fields in the pending object descriptor link list after SFNode replacement. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that reassigns a single-node field, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory, crashing the process and potentially corrupting the heap.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in load_xmt_done() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that reads freed nodes during XMT parser teardown. Attackers can craft an XMT scene with a scene replace command that destroys PROTO sub-graphs, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting heap memory when opened.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in gf_event_target_get_node() because destroyed node event targets remain in media object lists. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with nodes such as InputSensor to trigger freed memory reads during gf_scene_disconnect(), crashing the process or corrupting heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_del that allows attackers to free PROTOs still owned by another scene command via the GF_SG_PROTO_DELETE handler. Attackers can craft an XMT scene that declares a PROTO in one command and deletes it by ID in another, crashing MP4Box and corrupting heap memory when opened.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that allows scene commands to reference PROTO sub-graph nodes freed by a scene replace command. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file that causes gf_node_get_field() and gf_node_unregister() to access freed memory, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting heap memory.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in WPMU DEV Forminator forminator allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Forminator: from n/a through 1.58.4.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Boone Gorges BuddyPress Docs buddypress-docs allows Stored XSS.This issue affects BuddyPress Docs: from n/a through 2.2.7.

MemberPress Members before 3.3.1, with the Block Permissions add-on enabled, contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated Author-level users to crash pages by saving a non-string blockPermissionsMessage block attribute. Attackers can store a JSON array in the attribute so wpautop() in get_block_replacement_content() throws a PHP 8 TypeError, causing fatal errors on post, home, search, and REST pages for unauthorized viewers.

anacrolix/torrent before 1.62.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in Decoder.readOneValue in bencode/decode.go that allows attackers to crash the process by supplying deeply nested bencode data. Attackers can deliver crafted .torrent files or magnet link metadata with millions of nested lists to cause a fatal stack overflow, or deeply nested v2 file trees to exhaust CPU.
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in weDevs Dokan dokan-lite allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Dokan: from n/a through 5.3.4.

HedgeDoc before 1.12.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the POST /history/:noteId endpoint that allows authenticated users to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ as the noteId. Attackers can send a pinned value to /history/__proto__, which historyPost() in lib/history.js assigns onto the prototype, crashing the Node.js process and causing denial of service for all users.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to evade stricter ProxyAuth domain rules by sending percent-encoded path separators. Attackers can request paths with encoded slashes, backslashes, semicolons, or dot segments that match a broader rule, reaching restricted paths once the reverse proxy or backend decodes them.

OpenOLAT 20.2.2 before 20.3.12, 21.0.0 before 21.0.7, and 21.1.0 before 21.1.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the TranscodingDeliveryDispatcher notifyResult callback endpoint. Unauthenticated attackers can POST crafted TranscoderJobResult JSON with attacker-supplied URLs to overwrite transcoded video and audio files and force server-side requests.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a path traversal (zip slip) vulnerability in ImportService#unzip_photos_file that allows authenticated users to write files outside the extraction folder. Attackers can upload a crafted photos zip archive during account import with ../ entry names to create new files at arbitrary locations writable by the diaspora* process.

oasdiff 1.24.0 before 1.34.1 fails to enforce --allow-external-refs=false when --open is used, because the recordingReader() capture reader in load/capture.go never applies the external-reference policy. Attackers supplying an untrusted OpenAPI spec can use external $ref values to read local files or trigger HTTP requests, with contents uploaded in the review bundle.

Delta Sharing reference server 1.4.0 before 1.5.0 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows share recipients to read unshared data via container-scoped Azure SAS tokens. Recipients with a valid bearer token can request credentials from the temporary-table-credentials endpoint to read every blob in the storage container, including unshared tables.

Gradio 6.27.0 before 6.32.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in gradio/history.py that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to use the operator's locally saved Hugging Face token by sending a forged Host: localhost header. When ssr_mode is enabled, requests proxied through the local Node SSR server pass the loopback check, letting attackers call run history endpoints to list buckets, read records and assets, and write buckets under the operator's account.

Umami 3.3.0 before 3.5.0 contains a race condition in two-factor authentication attempt limiting that allows attackers holding a user's password to bypass lockout. Attackers can send many concurrent POST requests to /api/2fa/verify that pass checkRateLimit before recordFailedAttempt runs, brute-forcing TOTP or backup codes beyond the five-attempt limit.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that uses NORMAL and TEXCOORD accessors without comparing their counts to the POSITION vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with shorter normal or texture coordinate arrays to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads and writes that crash the importing application.

A vulnerability was found in DumbWareio DumbDrop up to ff8f813f493e89c7da056e7a3101ce2ef48e3960. Affected by this vulnerability is the function isPathWithinUploadDir of the file src/routes/files.js of the component Files API. The manipulation results in improper access controls. The attack may be launched remotely. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
ZTE Z80 Ultra is affected by an unauthorized access vulnerability. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could result in an impact on integrity.

An authenticated attacker must reach the Edge file APIs through the Leader or directly on an Edge node. On affected managed Edge deployments with RBAC, Read Only access permits these calls. Disclosure is limited to files readable by the Edge process under its operating-system permissions and capabilities.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD server. A remote attacker can crash a multi-export NBD server process by exploiting stale metadata export state during an extended BLOCK_STATUS request, resulting in an assertion failure and denial of service.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD server. A remote attacker can crash qemu-nbd, qemu-storage-daemon, or qemu-system by sending NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT or NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT with a declared option length exceeding the actual payload, triggering an assertion failure and denial of service.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD block driver. A malicious NBD server can send an incomplete structured read reply marked as done, causing QEMU to return uninitialized host heap memory to the guest VM, resulting in host memory disclosure.

Missing authorization vulnerability in the "GetByProject" endpoint (/Project/{id}) of the VulnController in Cervantes version v1.3-beta could allow an authenticated attacker with VulnsRead permission to retrieve the vulnerabilities of any project, even without being a member of it, by supplying an arbitrary project ID.

PagePdfDocumentReader and ParagraphPdfDocumentReader are vulnerable to a denial of service when processing untrusted PDF input.



 The underlying text extraction logic reconstructs layout from a PDF's glyph positions and limits how much memory can be allocated for any single computed gap, but does not limit the cumulative allocation across an entire page.



A specially crafted PDF can exploit this to force excessive memory allocation during processing, resulting in OutOfMemoryError.



Depending on JVM configuration, this can cause request failures with degraded service under repeated exploitation, or immediate JVM termination when ExitOnOutOfMemoryError options are used.



Any application that processes PDFs from untrusted sources (document upload, email attachment processing, RAG ingestion, web crawling) using either affected reader is impacted.

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.13, 11.10.x <= 11.10.3, 11.11.x <= 11.11.3 fail to verify that the requesting user has file download permission under an ABAC policy before reading file content, which allows an authenticated channel member to obtain the contents of files they are denied access to via interactions with an Agent bot.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00759

A bug related to the Zookeeper HTTP endpoints in Apache Solr allows an authenticated attacker with zk-read permission to read /security.json, bypassing the security-read authorization check. This may cause unauthorized read of credential hashes and authorization configuration.

For this attack to be successful, the following must be true
  *  The system is secured with Solr's Basic Auth plugin
  *  The attacker has gained direct network access to the Solr cluster
  *  The attacker has obtained credentials for a user account with zk-read permission (which is recommended assigned to trusted admins only)


Users are recommended to upgrade to 9.11.0, 10.1.0 or a newer release.
Users who cannot upgrade immediately are recommended to assign the zk-read permission only to users who they entrust reading security.json.

Improper authentication in the emergency login in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an attacker who holds an administrator emergency code to create multiple persistent administrator sessions via replay of the single-use code on the scripting login endpoint.

Improper access control in the access request approval endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated low-privileged user to self-approve a credential access request via a client-controlled parent request identifier.

Medplum server 5.1.4 before 5.1.42 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Binary $presigned-url operation that allows non-admin project members to overwrite other projects' Binary content. Attackers in a project linked to another project can request a signed upload URL with upload=true for a readable Binary and overwrite its stored content, since project ownership is never verified.

msgpack-c C++ library cpp-3.0.0 through cpp-9.0.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the Boost.X3 parser in include/msgpack/v2/x3_parse.hpp when built with MSGPACK_USE_X3_PARSE in reference mode. Attackers can supply crafted msgpack input parsed over buffering iterators so decoded str, bin and ext objects hold dangling pointers, disclosing freed heap memory or crashing the process.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache IoTDB. Authenticated REST clients can bypass row-limit cap to triggerheap-exhaustion DoS.



This issue affects Apache IoTDB: from 0.13.0 before 2.0.12.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.12, which fixes the issue.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache IoTDB. Authenticated Grafana clients can bypass row-limit cap to trigger heap-exhaustion DoS.



This issue affects Apache IoTDB: from 0.13.0 through 2.0.11.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.12, which fixes the issue.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache IoTDB. Authenticated REST clients can insert large payload to trigger heap-exhaustion DoS.



This issue affects Apache IoTDB: from 0.13.0 through 2.0.11.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.12, which fixes the issue.

ToDesktop Builder before 0.36.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the todesktop-fs custom protocol handler that allows attackers to escape the bundled files directory using ../ sequences. Attackers who can run script in an application's renderer can issue XMLHttpRequest calls with traversal paths to read arbitrary files accessible to the user.

ServerOS Panel before 1.10.1 contains a decompression bomb vulnerability in DeploySourcePacker::extract() that allows authenticated users with manage-machines permission to bypass the 4 GB unpacked-size limit by under-declaring zip entry sizes. Attackers can upload a crafted archive via POST /machines/{machine}/sources whose entries inflate far beyond declared sizes, filling the host disk and denying service to all workspaces.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not check the token state that GSSContext.unwrap() reports on a GSS-encrypted connection. An attacker on the network path can replay an earlier server packet from the same connection, and the driver accepts it as the answer to the current query. The driver also shares one MessageProp between reading and writing. One integrity-only packet from the server then makes the driver send later SQL and parameters without encryption. Only connections with gssEncMode=prefer or require that start GSS encryption are affected. Versions 42.2.15 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, cuts the weight and scale of a BigDecimal to 16 bits when it sends the value in binary, which is the default. The server then stores a different number without an error. For example 999999.99e-262144 is stored as 999999.99, so a tiny value can pass a range check and be stored as a large one. The driver also computes 10 to the power of the scale first, so a short value such as 1e-200000000 keeps a thread busy for minutes. Versions 42.3.0 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the MPL multicast engine that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt memory via unchecked seed ID lengths. Attackers can send near-maximum-size MPL messages with an S=3 option in a short hop-by-hop header, causing data_message_expiration() to write 16 bytes past uip_buf and crash the node.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in icmp_in() in os/net/ipv6/multicast/mpl.c that allows unauthenticated attackers to hang nodes via crafted MPL control messages. Attackers on the same link can send an MPL data message to create a seed entry, then an all-zero bit vector control message causing index wraparound and denial of service.

Convoy before 26.3.7 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows any project API key holder, including viewer-scoped keys, to read host files via require() in JavaScript transform functions. Attackers can submit a function to the sources/test_function endpoint calling require on a file path to disclose configuration files containing database credentials and secrets.

sdcb Chats 1.10.0 before 1.17.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in GetAssignedUserDetails that allows assigned non-admin users to read other users' per-user MCP headers. Attackers can request the assigned-user-details endpoint to obtain bearer tokens in CustomHeaders and impersonate other users against the downstream MCP server.

The Intel SoC FPGA Agilex5 SoC's static MMU region table in soc/intel/intel_socfpga/agilex5/mmu_regions.c mapped the System Manager peripheral (sysmgr) with MT_P_RW_U_RW. That sets the EL0 access-permission bit in the page-table descriptor, so user mode can read and write the block. The other peripheral windows in the same table, and the same block on the sibling Agilex SoC, are correctly mapped MT_P_RW_U_NA.

On arm64, memory-domain page tables are cloned from the kernel page tables (arch_mem_domain_init()). When CONFIG_USERSPACE is enabled, every user mode thread therefore gets direct load/store access to the System Manager registers, with no partition grant or system call. Any untrusted code running as a user thread can exploit this.

The System Manager controls system-wide state that only the kernel should own: NoC/FPGA-bridge idle requests, SDMMC and EMAC interface configuration, FPGA interface enables and boot scratch registers. A user thread can stall the interconnect or reconfigure peripherals out from under kernel drivers, causing denial of service and integrity loss for the platform, and can read that configuration. This breaks the userspace isolation boundary. Builds without CONFIG_USERSPACE (the default) are not affected. The fix maps the region MT_P_RW_U_NA.

The STM32 SMBus driver (drivers/smbus/smbus_stm32.c) implements smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() by issuing a single i2c_transfer() in which the byte-count byte returned by the peripheral is read directly into the len field of the following i2c_msg. That message then receives data straight into the caller-supplied buffer. Nothing bounds the count, so smbus_stm32_block_read() and smbus_stm32_block_pcall() read up to 255 bytes into a buffer that the SMBus API documents (and the syscall verifiers validate) as holding at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes.

The count is chosen by the addressed SMBus peripheral. A malicious, counterfeit or faulty device on the bus (for example a removable smart battery, PMBus supply or plug-in module), or anyone able to drive the bus lines, can report a block count above 32 and cause the driver to write up to 223 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer. Callers typically pass a 32-byte stack buffer, as the in-tree smbus block_read shell command does, so the overflow lands on the caller's stack before any caller-side count check can run.

The result is attacker-controlled stack or memory corruption in the context of the calling thread, which can crash the system or potentially be leveraged for code execution. When the call arrives through the smbus_block_read/smbus_block_pcall system calls, the out-of-bounds write happens in supervisor mode beyond the 32-byte region validated for the user thread. The fix receives the block into a driver-local 255-byte buffer and copies it out only when the count is at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX, returning -ENODATA otherwise.

DreameHome cloud API before 2026-10-14 contained an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the POST /smart-app/meari-cloud/redirectAndLogin endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to obtain another user's Meari camera-platform identity and session credentials by supplying that user's uid. The endpoint used the caller-supplied uid to select the Meari account without verifying that it belonged to the account authenticated by the Dreame-Auth token. Attackers can obtain target uids through public forum profiles and an email-to-uid lookup, and use the leaked credentials to access live video, microphone audio, the camera speaker, and stored recordings of Meari-backed cameras.

DreameHome MQTT broker before 2026-10-26 contained an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to subscribe to another device's status topic /status/{DID}/{UID}/{model}/# without owning or having access to the device. Attackers who know the device DID, owner UID, and model can receive the device's telemetry, including compressed LiDAR map frames exposing the home's layout, the Wi-Fi SSID and BSSID, local IP address, gateway, firmware version, and the session key used for encrypted video.

DreameHome device sharing and MQTT broker before 2026-10-26 contained an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows former share recipients to keep receiving a device's MQTT status messages after the owner revokes sharing. Revocation removed application access and the device-command API rejected the former recipient, but the broker still accepted subscriptions to the device's status topic using the DID, owner UID, and model exposed during sharing, allowing continued monitoring of the home's map data and device status.

DreameHome for Android (com.dreame.smartlife) before 2.6.4.0 contains a download of code without integrity check vulnerability in RnPluginDownloadManager.java that allows network-positioned attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript within the application by replacing React Native feature bundles that are only validated against a client-stored MD5 checksum without publisher authentication. Attackers can replace both the downloaded bundle and its corresponding MD5 metadata to run modified code with the application's permissions and access to its bridge APIs.

An out-of-bounds write issue exists in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC. It affects applications that decrypt CBC or ECB ciphertext with PKCS7 padding over multiple calls into the minimum documented output buffer. A remote user who supplies crafted ciphertext might crash the application or corrupt adjacent memory. Affected are all versions of AWS-LC before 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.x before 4.2.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x before 3.6.0, and AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x before 2.0.18.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS-LC 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.2.0, or AWS-LC-FIPS 3.6.0.



AWS-LC-FIPS 2.0.18 is also fixed; AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x reaches end of support in April 2027.

Missing authorization in Kibana Security AI Assistant conversation deletion can allow an authenticated user with access to the assistant to delete other users' conversations in the same space. The delete-all operation can issue a query without an ownership filter using the assistant's internal Elasticsearch client. A user can consequently delete conversation history that they do not own or have permission to modify.

Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value (CWE-789) in Packetbeat can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted, malformed Cassandra protocol message. An unauthenticated attacker who can send traffic on a network segment that Packetbeat monitors can cause Packetbeat to allocate excessive memory and terminate. Elastic Agent is also affected when the Network Packet Capture integration monitors Cassandra traffic, because it uses the same protocol decoder.

Uncontrolled resource allocation in Kibana exception-list filter creation can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with access to the Security solution can submit a specially crafted request containing a large number of exception-list identifiers. Kibana can create an unbounded number of concurrent operations while resolving those identifiers, exhausting memory and crashing the Kibana process.

Certain Fleet APIs in Kibana expose stored credentials to authenticated users who do not have the Fleet Settings: Read privilege. For example, a user with the Fleet Agent policies: Read privilege can retrieve credentials through Fleet output and agent binary download source APIs. The disclosed credentials could allow the attacker to authenticate to connected backend systems.

Uncontrolled resource consumption in Elasticsearch query parsing can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with search permissions can submit a specially crafted query containing an excessive number of clauses. Expanding those clauses in memory before enforcing query complexity limits can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node.

Unconstrained S3 endpoint settings in Elasticsearch ES|QL data sources can cause requests containing storage credentials to be sent to an attacker-controlled host. A user with data-source management privileges can configure a custom endpoint without the intended host restriction. On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only.

A relative path traversal vulnerability in Kibana Fleet and Elastic Agent allows an authenticated user with both Fleet Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges to distribute a malicious integration policy to managed Elastic Agents. A vulnerable Elastic Agent processing that policy for a component that runs in an isolated unit can modify or delete files outside the component's intended runtime directory with the privileges of the Elastic Agent process. This can cause loss of files or persistent denial of service on affected hosts.

Missing authorization in Kibana Security AI Assistant conversation deletion can allow an authenticated assistant user to permanently delete a shared or global conversation owned by another user in the same space. The individual-delete path can treat read access to a shared conversation as permission to delete it without checking ownership. The deleted conversation history is lost to its legitimate owner.

An issue was discovered in Elasticsearch where specially crafted compressed payloads can cause an infinite loop. A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a malformed payload to a product API endpoint that causes the node to enter a permanent CPU loop, occupying a request-processing thread indefinitely. This can progressively exhaust the node's processing capacity, degrading or denying access to product features, and requiring a restart of the affected node to recover.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4bf95a3, contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the GET /dashboard/surveys endpoint that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to infer data from the main application database. SurveyService inserts unrecognized sort values directly into the ORDER BY clause of a native query, so attackers can supply SQL expressions and use response timing to infer any data readable by the application's database account, including data outside the surveys listed on their dashboard.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.9.0, nested tools invoked by OrchestratorBlock bypass the main execution queue and are charged only after succeeding, but post-run billing still refunds a failed tool's catalogue price as a presumed pre-flight charge. Any authenticated customer can trigger failed nested calls to add uncharged credits to their balance and fund later executions using the operator's credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. Prior to 8.5.0, the staff-facing portal endpoints GET api/onsiteactivityviews and GET api/onsiteactivityview/{id}, mapped to OnsiteActivityView.Query and OnsiteActivityView.Read with p_acl = p_none in portal/patient/_app_config.php, are handled without an authorization check for an authenticated staff session whose bootstrap_pid is empty. portal/patient/_machine_config.php admits that authenticated staff session, and portal/patient/fwk/libs/verysimple/Phreeze/GenericRouter.php applies the route ACL only when bootstrap_pid is nonempty, so the staff request bypasses the p_none check. OnsiteActivityViewController::Query() returns records without patient scoping, and OnsiteActivityViewController::Read() loads a record by identifier without checking ACL or ownership; OnsiteActivityViewReporter::GetCustomQuery() joins portal activity to patient demographics and includes names, dates of birth, addresses, and Social Security numbers. Any authenticated staff account, including one without the patients/demo permission, can therefore read sensitive demographics for patients represented by an existing onsite_portal_activity row; at least one such row must exist for the endpoint to return patient data. This issue is fixed in version 8.5.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.4.4, addFromUrl() in src/Flame/Database/Attach/Media.php performs an outbound HTTP request to a caller-supplied URL and stores the response without validating the URL scheme or destination, which could enable server-side request forgery if a reachable feature passes attacker-controlled URLs to the method. The maintainer reports that no shipped first-party feature calls this method and that it is currently unreachable through product functionality, so no current attack path or impact was identified. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.4.
Tanium addressed an information disclosure vulnerability.
Tanium addressed an insertion of sensitive information into log file vulnerability in Connect.
Tanium addressed a denial of service vulnerability in Tanium Server.

rConfig Core 8.1.0 before 8.2.20 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a missing authorization vulnerability in ExportController.php that allows authenticated users to export restricted tables. Attackers can supply excluded table names to export($table), bypassing the EXCLUDED_TABLES deny list, and obtain decrypted passwords, device credentials, and API tokens.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in build_frame_code() in libavformat/nutenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt the header_len[] array by supplying inputs with many audio streams. Attackers can remux a crafted input with many audio streams to NUT, causing out-of-bounds reads past static header tables and crashing the application.

FFmpeg through 9.1 contains an insecure default configuration in the zmq and azmq filters of libavfilter/f_zmq.c that binds an unauthenticated command socket to all interfaces on TCP port 5555. Remote attackers can send 'TARGET COMMAND [ARG]' messages passed to avfilter_graph_send_command() to change filter runtime parameters and alter processed audio or video.

FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_scale.c that allows attackers to read past the filter input array by sending width or height commands using ref variables. Attackers can send such commands via sendcmd scripts or unauthenticated zmq or azmq filters, causing config_props() to dereference an invalid pointer and crash the process.
An off-by-one error in String::WriteOneByte() in Samsung lwnode can cause a one-byte out-of-bounds write when copying a UTF-16 string

In Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK versions 2.0.0-milestone-10 to 2.0.0-milestone-16, the destination validation of the Operation Delegation feature, introduced to prevent server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-7412), can be bypassed through DNS rebinding.



Before dispatching a delegated Operation invocation, the server resolves the host of the `invocationDelegation` qualifier URI and rejects loopback, private, link-local, multicast and cloud metadata addresses. The outbound HTTP client (Reactor Netty), however, performs its own, independent DNS lookup when opening the connection and does not use the validated addresses. An attacker who can create or update a Submodel Operation and controls the DNS records of the delegation host can answer the validation lookup with a public address and the connection lookup with an internal address. No authentication is required when the authorization feature is not enabled.



Invoking the Operation then causes the BaSyx server to send HTTP POST requests to destinations the protection is meant to block, such as services in internal IT/OT networks, loopback-only interfaces, or cloud metadata endpoints. The server can be used to pivot into network segments that are not directly reachable by the attacker.



Only deployments with the Operation Delegation feature enabled are affected. The feature is enabled by default.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK 2.0.0-milestone-17.

This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.1 before v14.08.5.
